title: Asymmetric S&P 500 reactions to CPI surprises in a high-inflation environment
snippet:
# Asymmetric S&P 500 reactions to CPI surprises in a high-inflation environment
...
This paper examines short-term equity market reactions to U.S. Consumer Price Index (CPI) announcements during the high-inflation regime of 2021–2025. Using an event study with the Constant Mean Return Model and daily S&P 500 returns, we document a pronounced asymmetry. Positive surprises (actual CPI below expectations) generate large and statistically significant abnormal returns across all event windows, with CARs exceeding 1%. In contrast, negative surprises (actual CPI above expectations) produce negative abnormal returns of similar magnitude but without statistical significance. Neutral announcements show no robust effects. These findings demonstrate that equity market sensitivity to CPI news is strongly regime-dependent and asymmetric, with disinflationary signals driving the most pronounced market reactions.

for financial markets. Using LSEG Tick History data, we analyse seven major CPI surprise events and measure market reactions at the millisecond level.

We define a major CPI surprise as a deviation of at least 0.3% between expected and actual year-on-year CPI. While the analysis spans data over a 12-year timeframe, all such events identified occurred during 2021 and 2022, reflecting heightened inflation volatility and reduced forecast accuracy in the post-pandemic period.

• CPI surprises trigger immediate repricing across asset classes. 
• US 10-year Treasury yields react most strongly, rising by an average of 2.8 basis points following upside inflation surprises. 
• S&P 500 futures experience an average decline of 0.31% following higher-than-expected inflation releases. 
• Larger inflation surprises are generally associated with larger market reactions.

Understanding how markets react in the seconds immediately following an economic surprise requires access to high frequency historical market data. LSEG Tick History enables analysis of price formation, liquidity dynamics and cross asset market reactions at millisecond resolution across global markets. For this study, we use LSEG Tick History to examine how major CPI surprises affected US Treasury yields and S&P 500 futures immediately after publication. The analysis demonstrates how high-frequency historical data can reveal market behaviour that is not visible in traditional end-of-day datasets.
